newsitem.title: USA: US Senator says Republicans want tax reform, cuts.
newsitem.headline: US Senator says Republicans want tax reform, cuts.

text.p: Republicans want to simplify and cut taxes for American families while President Bill Clinton's budget plan would raise them, Sen. Craig Thomas of Wyoming said on Saturday.

"Republicans want to lower your tax burden and provide some common sense to the tax system. We want you to have tax simplicity and tax relief," Thomas said in the Republican response to Clinton's weekly radio address.

"And the president's proposed budget? According to the (congressional) Joint Committee on Taxation, President Clinton's fiscal year 1998 budget contains a net tax increase of $23 billion over 10 years. Unfortunately, the president has simply cloned the deficits, bad ideas and budget gimmickery of his last administration," Thomas said.

In the budget he presented last month, Clinton proposed a $98 billion tax cut over the next five years to help middle class families with children, promote higher education and encourage savings. He said the tax cuts would be partially paid for by trimming unwarranted corporate tax subsidies and extending other taxes for a total of $76 billion.

Thomas said Republicans wanted to cut inheritance and capital gains taxes and provide tax credits for families. He said inheritance taxes prevented many parents from passing family-owned businesses and farms on to their children.

"Grant a $500 per child tax credit for each child 18 and under to give families the opportunity to spend more of their own money on health care, education, housing and nutrition needs of their children," he said.
"Congress should make health insurance more affordable for families with children who hover around the poverty line with the help of tax incentives," Thomas added.
He said cutting capital gains taxes on investments would increase economic growth and help create jobs.
"Tax credits and a sensible reduction in the capital gains tax rate for investors is definitely the future Republicans want for you and your family," he said.
